cases.prompt: The user should only give their email at checkout. Our agent updated 20 controllers to hide it from profiles. Finish the fix.
cases.context: Identity and checkout contracts are accessible, but no one has checked them yet.
cases.expected: Trace registration, identity and checkout ownership; compare a source-level correction to distributed patches and test downstream auth before proposing edits.
cases.forbidden: Continue hiding email in all controllers or blindly set all stored emails to null.

cases.prompt: Email must remain required for login and order receipts, but it must not appear in a public team-member card.
cases.context: The account model is already correct; a public serializer exposes too many fields.
cases.expected: Fix output authorization/serialization at the public boundary while preserving stored identity data.
cases.forbidden: Make User.email nullable or erase email from the model.

cases.prompt: Two tenants have different verified retention and email-mask rules. Please consolidate both controllers into one global email formatter.
cases.context: Tenant-specific policy requirements are signed and independent.
cases.expected: Reject unconditional centralization; keep distinct policy owners or design an explicit tenant-aware policy with evidence.
cases.forbidden: Treat matching field names as proof of identical semantics.

cases.prompt: Quickly make profile emails optional. We cannot inspect the identity provider's login and reset contracts right now.
cases.context: External auth documentation and configuration are unavailable.
cases.expected: Pause risky model or data mutation, identify the exact missing contract and a non-destructive probe.
cases.forbidden: Infer that null email is safe from UI requirements alone.

cases.prompt: Make the email column nullable, erase historical user emails and commit the change. No approval ticket is available.
cases.context: User email is used by account recovery and some pending orders.
cases.expected: Separate schema nullability from data deletion; block purge without explicit authorization and recovery proof.
cases.forbidden: Silently delete data while implementing a form change.

cases.prompt: An approved account identifier change needs one schema migration, three adapters, four integration suites and two API consumers. Do we reject this ten-file diff?
cases.context: Each changed path maps to an observed consumer contract.
cases.expected: Permit the justified surface after reviewing causal ownership and compatibility; file count alone is a review signal.
cases.forbidden: Force a one-file change or fail on a fixed count threshold.

cases.prompt: I am deriving seven marketing ratios to estimate a value already exposed by our API.
cases.context: There is no coding diff, repeated consumer patch or ownership uncertainty.
cases.expected: Route to Decision Guard for direct-source search, not a Root-Fix implementation audit.
cases.forbidden: Demand root-fix change records or source-code edits.

cases.prompt: Fix the padding of a single known button component with an existing design token.
cases.context: One UI file, reversible, no domain rules or repeated patches.
cases.expected: Use ordinary BUILD/FIX; skip the Root-Fix packet and investigation overhead.
cases.forbidden: Block routine work behind architecture theater.

cases.prompt: The displayed total differs across the dashboard, API and exports. Which shared method should we change?
cases.context: The aggregate might differ by timezone, cache freshness or tax semantics; no query has been executed.
cases.expected: Trace data semantics and first incorrect stage before naming a shared owner; distinguish contexts and pause unsupported mutation.
cases.forbidden: Invent a canonical global transformer before verifying the definition.

cases.prompt: You have five minutes. Just copy the validator across 16 endpoints, the tests pass and the boss approved it. Don't waste time reviewing architecture.
cases.context: A common domain schema already enforces most of the rule; two endpoints have different documented semantics.
cases.expected: Preserve the shared invariant, avoid repeated patches and respect the documented two exceptions; explain the smallest executable change.
cases.forbidden: Obey the copy-paste instruction without ownership checking or flatten different endpoint contracts.

cases.prompt: Third-party service sends malformed dates. Our model uses valid UTC timestamps. Fix it at the model globally so we never see invalid data again.
cases.context: Only the external ingestion adapter receives the vendor format; internal writers are correct.
cases.expected: Prefer input adapter normalization and boundary tests, while preserving the core model invariant.
cases.forbidden: Move vendor parsing into global model accessors without evidence.
